title_en: Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (IV)

articles.content_en: Where shareholders, directors, supervisors, and others of a company request confirmation that a resolution of the shareholders' meeting, general meeting of shareholders, or board of directors is void or has not been established, the People's Court shall accept the case according to law.

Plaintiffs who request revocation of a resolution of the shareholders' meeting, general meeting of shareholders, or board of directors pursuant to Article 85 of the Civil Code and Article 22(2) of the Company Law shall have the status of a shareholder of the company at the time of prosecution.

In a case where the plaintiff requests confirmation that a resolution of the shareholders' meeting, general meeting of shareholders, or board of directors has not been established or is void, or requests revocation of the resolution, the company shall be listed as the defendant. Other interested parties involved in the resolution may be listed as third parties according to law.
Before the conclusion of the debate at the first-instance trial, other persons qualified as plaintiffs who apply to participate in the litigation prescribed in the preceding paragraph with the same claims may be listed as joint plaintiffs.

Where a shareholder requests revocation of a resolution of the shareholders' meeting, general meeting of shareholders, or board of directors, and the request complies with Article 85 of the Civil Code and Article 22(2) of the Company Law, the People's Court shall support it; however, if the meeting convening procedure or voting method has only minor defects and has not produced a substantive impact on the resolution, the People's Court shall not support it.

Where a resolution of the shareholders' meeting, general meeting of shareholders, or board of directors is confirmed void or revoked by a judgment of the People's Court, the civil legal relationship formed between the company and a bona fide counterparty pursuant to that resolution shall not be affected.

Where a shareholder, pursuant to Article 33 or Article 97 of the Company Law or the provisions of the company's articles of association, brings a prosecution requesting inspection or reproduction of specific company documents and materials, the People's Court shall accept the case according to law.
Where the company has evidence proving that the plaintiff prescribed in the preceding paragraph did not have the status of a company shareholder at the time of prosecution, the People's Court shall dismiss the prosecution, except where the plaintiff has preliminary evidence proving that his or her lawful rights and interests were damaged during the period of shareholding and requests inspection or reproduction of the company's specific documents and materials during the shareholding period according to law.

Where the company's articles of association, agreements among shareholders, or other instruments substantively deprive shareholders of the right to inspect or reproduce company documents and materials pursuant to Articles 33 and 97 of the Company Law, and the company refuses the shareholder's inspection or reproduction on that ground, the People's Court shall not support it.

When the People's Court hears a case in which a shareholder requests inspection or reproduction of specific company documents and materials, and supports the plaintiff's claims, it shall specify in the judgment the time, place, and list of the specific company documents and materials to be inspected or reproduced.
Where a shareholder inspects company documents and materials pursuant to an effective judgment of the People's Court, such inspection may be conducted with the assistance of accountants, lawyers, or other practicing personnel of intermediary institutions who have a confidentiality obligation according to law or pursuant to professional practice norms, in the presence of the shareholder.

Where a shareholder, after exercising the right to information, divulges the company's trade secrets, thereby damaging the company's lawful interests, and the company requests the shareholder to compensate for the relevant losses, the People's Court shall support it.
Where an accountant, lawyer, or other person who, pursuant to Article 10 of these Provisions, assists the shareholder in inspecting company documents and materials divulges the company's trade secrets, thereby damaging the company's lawful interests, and the company requests such person to compensate for the relevant losses, the People's Court shall support it.

Where directors, senior officers, and others of a company fail to perform their duties according to law, resulting in the company's failure to create or preserve the company documents and materials prescribed in Articles 33 and 97 of the Company Law, thereby causing losses to shareholders, and shareholders request, according to law, that the company's directors or senior officers who bear corresponding responsibility bear civil liability for compensation, the People's Court shall support it.

In a case where a shareholder requests the company to distribute profits, the company shall be listed as the defendant.
Before the conclusion of the debate at the first-instance trial, other shareholders who, based on the same distribution plan, request distribution of profits and apply to participate in the litigation shall be listed as joint plaintiffs.

Where a shareholder submits a valid resolution of the shareholders' meeting or general meeting of shareholders that contains a specific distribution plan and requests the company to distribute profits, and the company refuses to distribute profits and its defense that the resolution cannot be performed is not established, the People's Court shall adjudicate that the company shall distribute profits to the shareholder according to the specific distribution plan set forth in the resolution.

Where a shareholder does not submit a resolution of the shareholders' meeting or general meeting of shareholders that contains a specific distribution plan and requests the company to distribute profits, the People's Court shall reject his or her claims, except where, in violation of legal provisions, the shareholder abuses shareholder rights, causing the company not to distribute profits and thereby causing losses to other shareholders.

Where a natural-person shareholder of a limited liability company changes due to succession, and other shareholders assert the exercise of the right of first refusal pursuant to Article 71(3) of the Company Law, the People's Court shall not support it, except where the company's articles of association provide otherwise or all shareholders agree otherwise.

Where a shareholder of a limited liability company transfers equity to a person outside the shareholders, he or she shall notify other shareholders in writing or by other reasonable means by which receipt can be confirmed, for the purpose of seeking their consent, regarding the equity transfer matter. Where half or more of the other shareholders do not consent to the transfer, and the dissenting shareholders do not purchase the equity, the People's Court shall find that consent to the transfer is deemed to have been given.
Where equity is transferred with the consent of the shareholders, and other shareholders assert that the transferring shareholder shall notify them of the equal conditions for transferring the equity in writing or by other reasonable means by which receipt can be confirmed, the People's Court shall support it.
Where equity is transferred with the consent of the shareholders, under equal conditions, other shareholders other than the transferring shareholder assert their right of first refusal to purchase the equity, the People's Court shall support it, except where the transferring shareholder gives up the transfer pursuant to Article 20 of these Provisions.

When the People's Court determines whether the "equal conditions" as referred to in Article 71(3) of the Company Law and these Provisions are satisfied, it shall consider factors such as the quantity, price, payment method, and time limit of the transferred equity.

Where a shareholder of a limited liability company asserts the right of first refusal to purchase transferred equity, he or she shall, after receiving the notice, submit the purchase request within the exercise period prescribed in the company's articles of association. Where the company's articles of association do not prescribe an exercise period or the provisions are unclear, the period specified in the notice shall prevail; if the period specified in the notice is shorter than thirty days or the exercise period is not specified, the exercise period shall be thirty days.

Where a transferring shareholder of a limited liability company, after other shareholders have asserted the right of first refusal, no longer agrees to transfer the equity, the People's Court shall not support the other shareholders' assertion of the right of first refusal, except where the company's articles of association provide otherwise or all shareholders agree otherwise. Where other shareholders assert that the transferring shareholder shall compensate them for their reasonable losses, the People's Court shall support it.

Where a shareholder of a limited liability company transfers equity to a person outside the shareholders, fails to seek the opinions of the other shareholders on the equity transfer matter, or damages the other shareholders' right of first refusal by means of fraud, malicious collusion, or other means, and the other shareholders claim to purchase the transferred equity under equal conditions, the People's Court shall support it, except where the other shareholders have not made such claim within thirty days from the date on which they knew or should have known the equal conditions for exercising the right of first refusal, or where more than one year has elapsed from the date of equity change registration.
Where the other shareholders prescribed in the preceding paragraph only raise requests such as confirmation of the validity of the equity transfer contract and the effectiveness of the equity change, without simultaneously claiming to purchase the transferred equity under equal conditions, the People's Court shall not support it, except where the other shareholders are unable to exercise the right of first refusal for reasons not attributable to themselves and request damages.
Where an equity transferee outside the shareholders is unable to achieve the purpose of the contract because a shareholder exercises the right of first refusal, he or she may request the transferring shareholder to bear corresponding civil liability according to law.

Where equity of a limited liability company is transferred to a person outside the shareholders by auction, when the "written notice," "notice," and "equal conditions" prescribed in Article 71(2) and (3) or Article 72 of the Company Law are applied, they shall be determined in accordance with relevant laws and judicial interpretations.
Where state-owned equity of a limited liability company is transferred at a property rights exchange established according to law, when the "written notice," "notice," and "equal conditions" prescribed in Article 71(2) and (3) or Article 72 of the Company Law are applied, the trading rules of the property rights exchange may be referred to.

Where the supervisory board, or the supervisor of a limited liability company without a supervisory board, brings a lawsuit against a director or senior officer pursuant to Article 151(1) of the Company Law, the company shall be listed as the plaintiff, and the chairman of the supervisory board, or the supervisor of a limited liability company without a supervisory board, shall represent the company in the litigation according to law.
Where the board of directors, or the executive director of a limited liability company without a board of directors, brings a lawsuit against a supervisor pursuant to Article 151(1) of the Company Law, or brings a lawsuit against another person pursuant to Article 151(3) of the Company Law, the company shall be listed as the plaintiff, and the chairman of the board of directors or the executive director shall represent the company in the litigation according to law.

Where a shareholder who meets the conditions prescribed in Article 151(1) of the Company Law directly brings a lawsuit against a director, supervisor, senior officer, or another person pursuant to Article 151(2) and (3) of the Company Law, the company shall be listed as a third party to participate in the litigation.
Before the conclusion of the debate at the first-instance trial, other shareholders who meet the conditions prescribed in Article 151(1) of the Company Law and apply to participate in the litigation with the same claims shall be listed as joint plaintiffs.

In a case where a shareholder directly brings a lawsuit pursuant to Article 151(2) and (3) of the Company Law, the benefits from prevailing in the lawsuit shall belong to the company. Where the shareholder requests the defendant to bear civil liability directly to him or her, the People's Court shall not support it.

In a case where a shareholder directly brings a lawsuit pursuant to Article 151(2) and (3) of the Company Law, if his or her claims are partially or wholly supported by the People's Court, the company shall bear the reasonable expenses paid by the shareholder for participating in the litigation.

These Provisions shall come into force on September 1, 2017.
For cases that have not yet been finally adjudicated after these Provisions come into force, these Provisions shall apply; for cases that have already been finally adjudicated before these Provisions come into force, or cases retried under the trial supervision procedure, these Provisions shall not apply.
